thread:
emily_support: FYI escalating a paying customer (ticket #98421). They see frequent EventSource disconnects only on Safari. Happens across our hosted and their VPC setup. Customer says partial events, then reconnect loop. link: https://support.example/t/98421 :frowning:
charlie_eng: thanks — can you paste minimal repro + headers they see? sounds like CDN/304 or SW interaction from past cases. :thinking:
emily_support: here's the short repro steps they gave: 1) open webapp in Safari 15/16 on macOS 12/13 2) click 'start stream' 3) after ~10-40s last event sometimes truncated, then EventSource fires onerror and reconnects but reconnect returns 304 from CDN and client stalls. Happens more when user has extension or service worker enabled. They also saw intermittent 401s when their billing hit a paused state.
emily_support: customer provided the last server response headers (copied):
```
HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 14:12:03 GMT
Server: edge-cache
Vary: Authorization, Cookie, Origin
Cache-Control: max-age=3600, stale-while-revalidate=60
Connection: keep-alive
```
charlie_eng: ugh. 304 for an SSE endpoint is a red flag. SSE must be served as a fresh streaming response (no 304/304+cache). Edge should not cache `text/event-stream`. Do they have our route under a CDN rule that sets `Cache-Control`?
charlie_eng: ask them to check that the endpoint responds with `Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`, no `Content-Length`, and `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform`. Also ensure `Connection: keep-alive` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` are preserved by the CDN.
dave_sre: adding: if the CDN returns 304, Safari's EventSource implementation sometimes treats it as end-of-stream and doesn't resume properly (esp with service worker). SW may serve a cached 304-like response. Recommend disabling caching on SSE route and excluding from SW fetch handlers.
olivia_devex: sample minimal curl to show intended headers (won't stream but useful for headers):
```
curl -i -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Cache-Control: no-cache" \
  -H "Origin: https://app.customer.com" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/stream?session=abc"
```
olivia_devex: expected response head should look like:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.customer.com
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true   # only if they use withCredentials
Connection: keep-alive
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
```
emily_support: customer also noted the client was using an EventSource polyfill in some browsers. They said native Safari triggers the issue more often when the tab is backgrounded or device goes to sleep. With polyfill it reconnects but sometimes duplicates partial event.
charlie_eng: polyfills often buffer events differently. For Safari-specific flakiness, two-pronged approach: 1) server-side: ensure no caching or 304 responses, set `Cache-Control: no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0` for SSE endpoints; add `Vary` carefully — remove Authorization/Cookie from Vary if possible for SSE route. 2) client-side: prefer native EventSource; if polyfill required, make it de-dup partial events on reconnect (idempotency using `id:` in SSE).
dave_sre: operational fixes: extend LB idle timeout to >120s, ensure proxy doesn't close upstream after small idle. If using Cloud CDN, create a route rule: bypass cache for `/v1/streams/*` or set `Cache-Key` to vary only on path (not on auth) and set `Cache-Control: no-store` on origin.
emily_support: there was also an auth angle — they hit a billing pause which caused our auth service to start returning 401s for the token during reconnect attempts. That triggers client reconnect loops and lots of short-lived connections (increasing concurrency/latency). I've told CS to remove pause while we triage.
charlie_eng: 401s midstream are bad. On reconnect, the client may open new connections which the CDNs might handle differently and return cached responses. We should make auth failures return a short JSON error (401) consistently, but avoid returning 304 or cached content on auth failures. Also add a server-side check: if token invalid on SSE open, immediately send a `retry: 60000\nevent: auth_error\ndata: {"code":"auth_required"}\n\n` and then close to avoid noisy reconnects.
olivia_devex: suggested short-term mitigation for customer: 1) disable service worker (dev tools -> unregister) 2) ensure SSE route excluded from SW fetch handlers 3) set `Cache-Control: no-cache` at origin and purge any CDN rules for that path 4) if on Safari, add small keepalive pings every 15s (`:keepalive` comment lines) to keep connection active.
emily_support: I've sent instructions and asked for logs. Customer will run curl check + report headers. They've accepted temporary disabling of SW. CS has unpaused billing for now.
charlie_eng: once we get headers, we'll check edge logs for 304 origins and for downstream `x-cache` lines. If reproducible, we'll push an emergency rule to disable caching for that host+path and set `origin_cache_control` override. dave, can you pre-authorize that change?
dave_sre: pre-authorized for support ops to toggle `edge.cache.enabled=false` on `/v1/stream*` for that customer host. I'll also increase upstream keepalive to 180s and add a dashboard alert for `sse.connection.aborts` spike.
deploy_bot: deploy queued: edge-rule/disable-sse-cache -> staging (id: dr-1123). Will notify once applied.
emily_support: thanks all — I'll update ticket #98421 with the workaround steps and link to this thread. :thumbsup:
charlie_eng: thanks — also add a small note in docs about `Safari + CDN + Service Worker` triage steps so support has a checklist. olivia, can you draft a short KB?
olivia_devex: on it, I'll seed a KB titled "SSE disconnects in Safari — CDN & Service Worker checklist" and include the curl checks, headers, SW steps, and recommended server headers.
emily_support: closing loop here after we get logs. will reopen if it reappears after edge change.
